newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends down, cuts loss on weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends down, cuts loss on weather.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures finished the week on a down note but managed to cut steep losses late Friday on revised outlook of cold weather returning to the northwestern U.S.
"It started to firm up at the end," said a Houston trader.

Late Friday in the western cash market, December power delivered at the California-Oregon Border (COB) was offered at $24.50 a megawatt hour (MWh) and at the Palo Verde switchyard in Arizona at $23.50.

Softening natural gas prices in the West and Canada pressured the electricity complex lower, but losses were mitigated by Bonneville Power Administration's (BPA) withdrawal from selling daily power through Monday.
December COB futures settled down $1.20 at $24.30, off from the day's low at $23.80. January COB finished 99 cents lower to $22.69. Active deferred COB contracts ended 50 cents to $1.25 lower.
December PV futures settled down 90 cents at $23.25, trimming a $1.40 loss. January PV finished down $1.04 at $21.25. The rest of the PV months closed 55 cents to $1.35 lower.
Despite today's loss, December COB retained a net gain of $2.97 or 13.9 percent from week-ago's settlement, and December PV $4.50, or 24 percent.
Brokers and marketers were uncertain about the direction of the complex after this week's wild upswing.
"A lot depends on gas," another Houston trader said.
The latest six to 10 day forecasts showed below normal temperatures for most of the Pacific Northwest and the northern part of the Rocky Mountain region.
